title: Pre-Analysis — Trim Air Standard 3 with Valve-Integrated Sensing and Duct Boss Deletion
abstract: Pre-analysis of the third trim air regulation standard, which deletes the welded duct sensor boss, covering the inspection obligation it removes, the bulletin effectivity it invalidates and the cabin work it collides with in the same ceiling void.

sections.objective: Establish what the deletion of the welded duct sensor boss does to the published set and to the aircraft already carrying it. The design question, whether the flange can be machined in situ, sits with the design office; pre-analysis was asked the narrower question of what breaks when the boss goes away, which aircraft can no longer be enrolled in an existing bulletin, and what else is working in the same ceiling void.
sections.scope_note: The search covers ATA 21-60 as the primary chapter and 21-60-12 as secondary because the zone controller parameter set is re-scaled. ATA 21-20 was included because the distribution ducting carries the boss. ATA 25 was searched and excluded: the ceiling panels are removed for access but nothing in them is modified, with one exception recorded as a finding because it shares the working area. The search was limited to aircraft already at the standard 2 configuration, since a boss can only be deleted from an aircraft that has one.
sections.method_note: Entity linking was seeded from the four part numbers, the three FINs, the single drawing and the three zones on the candidate. Semantic similarity was run over titles, abstracts and reason text with two seed phrases about weld toe cracking at a pressurised duct boss and about deleting a sensing element from a duct. The crew-facing finding was produced by similarity alone; nothing in the entity graph connects the flight crew description of zone temperature selection to a valve carrying an internal element, and that is precisely the case the demo is meant to make.
sections.findings_summary: Six items are confirmed and one of them blocks. The blocking item is the supersession itself: the standard 2 configuration is what puts the boss on the aircraft, and the candidate cannot be embodied on anything else, so the whole population question is inherited rather than free. The pre-conversion inspection bulletin is invalidated in a subtle way: it exists to establish that a duct flange is fit to carry a welded boss, and on an aircraft where the boss is to be deleted the inspection has no subject, yet its effectivity still enrols that aircraft. The crew description of how a cabin zone responds was found by similarity alone and would have to be reviewed even though the loop performance is deliberately unchanged, because it describes the sensing arrangement. The cabin window frame repair scheme was surfaced by a shared zone and is a genuine access collision rather than a technical one: both need the same centre cabin stowage area opened. The parts figure and the installation task both carry the boss and require re-issue.
sections.next_steps: Obtain the design office position on in-situ flange machining before the scope is fixed, because it decides whether this is an overnight task or a base maintenance task. Ask in-service engineering to state what happens to aircraft whose duct section was replaced after a boss crack. Agree with the pre-conversion inspection bulletin owner how its effectivity is to be narrowed. Coordinate the ceiling access with the cabin window repair programme.

similarity_seeds: weld toe cracking at a boss welded into a pressurised duct flange
deleting a sensing element from a duct and moving it inside the valve body
cabin zone temperature selection described for the flight crew

tasks.title: Map the published content that assumes a duct-mounted sensor
Test the pre-conversion inspection effectivity against a boss-less standard
Screen the ceiling void for competing cabin work
Obtain the design office position on in-situ flange machining

expected_findings.rationale: The standard 2 configuration is what puts the welded boss on the aircraft. The candidate can only be embodied on an aircraft that already has one, so its population and its embodiment condition are inherited rather than free, and every open question about the standard 2 population becomes a question about this one.
expected_findings.resolution: Fix the candidate effectivity as post standard 2 and inherit the standard 2 population figures rather than restating them.

expected_findings.rationale: The pre-conversion inspection exists to establish that a duct flange is fit to carry a welded boss. On an aircraft where the boss is to be deleted the inspection has no subject, yet its effectivity still enrols that aircraft and an operator following the published set would perform it for nothing.
expected_findings.resolution: Narrow the inspection effectivity to exclude aircraft enrolled in the candidate, once the candidate effectivity is fixed.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew entry is written about selectors, zone settling time and heat load; the candidate is written about a sensing element, a machined flange face and a weld toe. The two share no part number, no FIN, no zone and no distinctive vocabulary, and only an embedding over the subject matter connects them.

expected_findings.rationale: The flight crew description of how a cabin zone responds explains where the system measures temperature. The candidate moves that measurement inside the valve, and although the loop performance is deliberately unchanged the description is no longer accurate.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a review of the crew entry with flight operations support and issue it with the maintenance content.

expected_findings.rationale: The cabin window frame land repair works in the same centre cabin stowage area and needs the same lining and reveal removed. The two documents have nothing technically in common; the collision is entirely one of access and of the cabin being open twice.
expected_findings.resolution: Coordinate the ceiling and lining access with the window repair programme so that an aircraft carrying both is scheduled once.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the two existing valve standards as alternates on separate sheets. A third standard with no duct boss needs a third sheet and a restated effectivity note.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a publication change request once the valve part number is fixed.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task sets the clamp torque sequence against the boss position and contains a step to connect the sensor harness at the boss. Both become meaningless on the third standard.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a publication change request and hold it for issue with the parts figure.

expected_non_findings.reason: Same chapter, same FINs and the same trim air valve vocabulary, but it fits the hardened seat carrier into the existing valve body. The candidate replaces the valve entirely and an aircraft that has this bulletin embodied is neither helped nor hindered by the deletion of the duct boss.

Returned by the similarity search on wording about hot air ducting, joint inspection and a cabin distribution run, but it inspects the air cycle machine on a different sub-chapter and shares no valve, no boss and no ceiling zone with the trim air distribution work.

type_data.conclusion: Not yet issued. One blocking item and one invalidated bulletin effectivity identified; the in-situ machining question is with the design office and governs the scope.
